implementation_notes: C++20 range adaptors are range adaptor closure objects; cppreference states that adaptors can be composed into pipelines, and the pipe operator passes the range as the first argument, so `raw | views::filter(...) | views::transform(...)` is the pipeline and its stages are the named adaptor expressions. Execution is driven by iteration, and the result is materialised with a terminal algorithm (ranges::fold_left) or, since C++23, ranges::to<Container>(). This replaces the hand-written Pipeline class; use the std::function stage list instead when the stages are heterogeneous over a single value or the toolchain has no ranges.
pitfalls: Views are lazy and non-owning: nothing executes before iteration, and a view that outlives the underlying range dangles.

transform_view may re-invoke the function per element for proxy iterators, and filter_view re-runs the predicate on every pass, so expensive or side-effecting stages must be materialised or cached first.
C++20 has no ranges::to, so collecting the result needs a hand-written copy; stateful stages (sort, reverse) also require the right range category or must run outside the pipeline.

variants.name: std::function stage list over one value (C++11)
variants.implementation_notes: Before ranges, a pipeline over a single value is a vector of type-erased stage callables invoked in a loop: std::function can store function pointers, lambda expressions, bind expressions and other function objects behind one signature (cppreference), so heterogeneous named stages sit in the same container and the driver moves the payload from stage to stage. This is the realization to pick when the stages are a runtime list, when each stage is a class with state, or when the project is pre-C++20; the price is one indirect call per stage and possible allocation when a lambda's capture is large.
pitfalls: std::function may allocate for larger captures and blocks inlining; a hot pipeline should use auto-returning lambdas or a template parameter pack instead.
The stage list is checked only at run time: swapping two entries whose types differ compiles and fails during execution.
Every stage must accept and return the same Data type, so heterogeneous in/out types force variant or any payloads and lose compile-time checking.
